newsitem.title: MEXICO: Britannia to start Mexico drilling in Feb.
newsitem.headline: Britannia to start Mexico drilling in Feb.

text.p: Vancouver-based Britannia Gold Corp will start a drilling program in February in the silver-rich region around Real De Catorce in the state of San Luis Potosi, a company official said here Monday.

Fred Felder said plans were to invest $2 million in the next 12 months, chiefly in a drilling program starting some time in February with a first phase of 3,500 meters and totaling 10,000 meters within a year.

Felder said Britannia was looking for around 2 million tonnes of ore in high grade ranges. He said the company had just raised $5.5 million in financing, much of which will be allocated to the Real De Catorce project.
Britannia acquired control of 2,000 hectares at Real de Catorce in December, including a 300 tonne per day processing plant.

Real De catorce is a legendary silver area. First mined in 1773, production there only finally halted in 1990 because of low grades and high costs due to inflation. Throughout its history, it produced 200 million ounces of silver from 9,000 tonnes of ore.

Felder said the aim would be to target areas and extensions of past structures that had not been fully explored. He said Britannia had located four target areas and did not discount processing tailings. "Working tailings would not be a primary objective, though," he said, estimating there were some 2 million tonnes of tailings there.
Felder said other exploration properties in Mexico under operation were its Chiconal project in Chiapas state and its Sierra Madre site in Oaxaca state.
